questions.question: DNA is described as a long chemical molecule made of two chains of smaller units. If a scientist breaks all the chemical bonds holding the two chains together but leaves the bonds within each chain intact, what would they observe?
options: The DNA would break down into individual small chemical units.
The DNA would separate into two distinct, intact single chains.
The DNA would remain a double helix but lose its chemical code.
The DNA would immediately form a single, longer continuous chain.

questions.question: A student extracts all of the genetic material from a single muscle cell of a mouse. Which of the following terms correctly describes the entire collection of DNA that has been extracted?
options: A gene
The genome
A chromosome
A double helix

questions.question: If you look at the structure of DNA as a ladder, what represents the "rungs" (links across the middle) and what represents the "sides" of the ladder?
options: The sides are the single chemical units; the rungs are the double helix spiral bonds.
The sides are the nuclear membranes; the rungs are the tightly packed chromosome fibres.
The sides are the two spiralled chemical chains; the rungs are the chemical links connecting them.
The sides are the genes; the rungs are the non-coding sections of DNA.

questions.question: A physical model of DNA made of plastic pieces is useful for showing how the two chains connect, but what is a limitation or weakness of using such a physical model?
options: It cannot show that DNA is composed of two chains spiralled in a double helix.
It cannot show the dynamic, chemical processes and reactions that occur when DNA is used by the cell.
It cannot represent the fact that DNA is stored inside the nucleus of eukaryotic cells.
It fails to show that genes contain instructions for inherited features.

questions.question: When extracting DNA from a kiwi fruit, why can we see the extracted DNA in our test tube with the naked eye, even though individual DNA molecules are far too small to be seen?
options: The DNA molecules expand and grow larger when they come into contact with cold alcohol.
The extraction process causes millions of microscopic DNA molecules to clump together.
The DNA molecules absorb the green pigment of the kiwi fruit, making them visible.
The filter paper aligns the individual strands so they reflect light together.

questions.question: How are the genome, DNA, and chromosomes physically organized within a eukaryotic cell?
options: The genome is a single gene that is divided into chromosomes made of small DNA molecules.
Chromosomes are made of tightly wound DNA molecules, which together make up the genome.
DNA is made of chromosomes that are packed together to form a genome.
Chromosomes are small units of the genome that are connected by DNA chains.

questions.question: If we compare the genetic material in a human skin cell to that in a bacterium, which of the following describes a key structural difference in how they are stored?
options: Human cells store 23 pairs of chromosomes in the nucleus, whereas bacteria store a single chromosome in the cytoplasm.
Human cells store 23 single chromosomes in the nucleus, whereas bacteria store 23 pairs in the cytoplasm.
Human cells store one chromosome in the nucleus, whereas bacteria store 23 pairs in the cytoplasm.
Human cells store chromosomes in the cytoplasm, whereas bacteria store them in the nucleus.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the relationship between a chromosome, a gene, and their functions?
options: A gene is a packed chromosome that controls the cell membrane's structure.
A chromosome is a small section of a gene that contains instructions for one specific feature.
A gene is a specific section of DNA on a chromosome that stores instructions for a particular feature or process.
A chromosome is the chemical unit that links the two chains of a gene together.

questions.question: If a scientist removes a section of "non-coding DNA" from an organism's genome, what is the most likely direct consequence?
options: The organism will completely lose the ability to inherit any traits from its parents.
The cell may lose the ability to control when or how specific genes are turned on and used.
The cell will immediately stop producing all chemical units that form the DNA chains.
The chromosomes will instantly unwind and spill out of the nucleus.

questions.question: A student is looking under a microscope at an unknown cell. They observe that the cell has a cytoplasm and a cell membrane, but no nucleus. Where would they find the genetic material of this organism?
options: Free-floating inside the cytoplasm, because it is a bacterium.
Bound inside a vacuole, because it is an animal cell.
Within the cell membrane, because it is a fungus.
No genetic material exists because cells without a nucleus do not have DNA.

questions.question: How does DNA act as an "instruction manual" for an organism's life processes and features?
options: The physical weight of the DNA molecules determines which features develop.
The specific sequence of smaller molecules along the DNA chains forms a code that the cell decodes to build features.
DNA molecules physically move to different parts of the body to form physical tissues like muscle and bone.
The double helix shape acts as a physical template that directly shapes the cells of the organism.

questions.question: Why do brothers and sisters from the same biological parents look similar to each other and to their parents, but are not identical?
options: They inherit genetic material from only one parent, but which parent they inherit it from is completely random.
They inherit different mixtures of genetic material from both parents, leading to shared but unique combinations of features.
They inherit all their features from their father, and their environment makes them look like their mother.
They inherit genetic material from both parents, but the material is identical for every child.

questions.question: Except in the case of identical twins, offspring of the same parents show variation. What is the biological reason for this variation among offspring?
options: Offspring receive different combinations of genes from their parents, creating unique genetic instructions.
Offspring change their genetic material after birth based on their environment.
Only one parent passes on genetic material, and it changes depending on the age of the parent.
The non-coding DNA completely overrides the genes during growth.

questions.question: During fertilisation, an egg cell and a sperm cell fuse. How does this process relate to heredity?
options: It allows environmental changes from the parents' lives to be copied into the offspring's cells.
It combines genetic material from both parents, passing on the instructions that determine the offspring's biological features.
It destroys the parents' original DNA so that the offspring can develop entirely new, random traits.
It converts non-coding DNA into active genes to ensure the offspring is a new species.

questions.question: A professional athlete trains hard and develops extremely strong muscles. If they have a child, why won't the child automatically be born with extremely strong muscles?
options: Muscle strength is not controlled by any genetic material.
Only features programmed by instructions in the genetic material can be inherited, not traits acquired through training.
Acquired traits are only passed on from the mother, not the father.
The child will inherit the strength, but only after they reach adulthood.

questions.question: Which of the following features is caused entirely by environmental factors and cannot be passed on to offspring?
options: A scar on a person's arm from a childhood accident
The natural colour of a person's eyes
The shape of a person's earlobes
Having a hereditary blood group

questions.question: A group of scientists is studying a plant. They find some plants have red flowers and some have green leaves with spots caused by a leaf-mining insect. How should these two features be classified?
options: Red flowers are genetic; insect spots are genetic.
Red flowers are environmental; insect spots are genetic.
Red flowers are genetic; insect spots are environmental.
Red flowers are environmental; insect spots are environmental.

questions.question: Why did it take from the discovery of DNA in 1869 until 1953 for scientists to work out its double helix structure?
options: Scientists had to wait until the 1950s for the technology to extract DNA from cells to be invented.
It required scientists to share different pieces of evidence, collaborate, and build physical models to interpret the clues.
No one believed DNA was important until 1953, so no research was conducted on it.
The structure of DNA actually changed over time due to evolution.

questions.question: What crucial evidence did Rosalind Franklin's team in London contribute to the discovery of the structure of DNA in 1952?
options: They built the first three-dimensional cardboard model of the double helix.
They proved that bacteria do not have a nucleus.
They used X-rays to capture an image that indicated the helical shape of DNA.
They extracted DNA from fruit for the very first time.

questions.question: How did James Watson and Francis Crick use the scientific work of others to complete their model of DNA?
options: They used the X-ray picture taken by Franklin's team to work out and build a physical model of the double helix structure.
They proved that Rosalind Franklin's X-ray images were completely incorrect and built a different model.
They used the image to show that DNA is a single straight chain without any links.
They used it to discover that DNA is stored in the cytoplasm of human cells.

questions.question: DNA is described as a long chemical polymer. Which of the following best describes the fundamental structure of this molecule?
options: A single long protein chain folded into a complex 3D shape.
Two separate chains made of smaller chemical units that are joined together.
A triple strand of lipid molecules connected by sugar bridges.
Multiple independent rings of carbohydrates linked by peptide bonds.

questions.question: A scientist sequences all of the DNA found within a single somatic cell of a rare fern species. What is the correct biological term for this complete set of DNA?
options: The proteome
The genotype
The genome
The karyotype

questions.question: When visualizing the physical shape of a DNA molecule, how are the two chains and their connections arranged?
options: They are arranged as a flat, ladder-like structure that remains completely straight.
They form a single tightly coiled spring with no links across the middle.
They are spiralled around each other in a double helix, with linking units bridging the middle.
They form a sphere where the chains cross randomly and tie into knots.

questions.question: Students are evaluating a physical model of DNA made from plastic beads and wire. Which of the following represents a limitation or weakness of using such a physical model?
options: It shows that DNA consists of repeating smaller units joined together.
It represents the overall double helix shape in a three-dimensional way.
It cannot show the actual chemical bonds, dynamic movement, or the scale of real atoms.
It helps students visualize how the two strands run in opposite directions.

questions.question: During a DNA extraction experiment, a student expects to see individual double helix molecules using a standard classroom magnifying glass. Why is this expectation incorrect?
options: Single DNA molecules are too small to be seen with the unaided eye; we can only see them when millions of molecules clump together.
DNA is a gas when extracted, so it cannot be viewed under any optical magnification.
The extraction process always breaks DNA down into single atoms which are invisible.
DNA only becomes visible when it reacts with oxygen and turns into a dark metal.

questions.question: In a fruit DNA extraction protocol, why is dishwashing liquid (detergent) mixed with salt and added to the crushed fruit before filtering?
options: To dye the DNA a bright color so it is easily visible in the filter paper.
To break open the cell and nuclear membranes to release the DNA.
To neutralize the natural sugars so they do not turn into alcohol.
To convert the DNA from a solid state into a dissolved gas.

questions.question: If we compare the genomes of a human, a banana plant, and a bacterium, which statement is most scientifically accurate?
options: They share no similarities because they belong to completely different kingdoms of life.
Their genomes contain the same total amount of DNA and identical gene sequences.
They all have genomes made of DNA, containing both unique sequences and some shared similarities.
Only humans have a genome; plants and bacteria store their genetic information as proteins.

questions.question: What is the structural relationship between DNA and chromosomes inside a eukaryotic cell?
options: Chromosomes are proteins that chemically digest DNA molecules when the cell needs energy.
DNA molecules are wound up and tightly packed into structures called chromosomes.
Chromosomes are small liquid droplets that float inside the double helix of DNA.
DNA is a temporary shield that wraps around chromosomes to protect them from light.

questions.question: How does the organization and location of genetic material in a human body cell compare to that in a bacterium?
options: Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes in the nucleus; bacteria have one chromosome stored in the cytoplasm.
Humans have a single circular chromosome in the cytoplasm; bacteria have 23 pairs in a nucleus.
Both human cells and bacteria store 23 pairs of chromosomes inside a well-defined nucleus.
Humans store genetic material in the cytoplasm; bacteria store it in a membrane-bound nucleus.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes what a gene is and its primary function?
options: A gene is a protein coat that protects the cell membrane from external chemicals.
A gene is a section of DNA on a chromosome that stores instructions for an inherited feature or life process.
A gene is a carbohydrate chain used by cells to store excess glucose.
A gene is the specialized liquid found inside the nucleus of plant cells.

questions.question: A large proportion of a eukaryotic genome consists of non-coding DNA. What is a primary function of these non-coding regions?
options: They are waste materials that the cell must eject during division.
They contain instructions that control when and how the information in genes is used.
They are converted directly into glucose to power cellular respiration.
They act as physical anchors that glue the cell to surrounding tissues.

questions.question: An alien life form is discovered to have cells containing a nucleus, cytoplasm, and cell membrane. In which of these structures would you expect to find its genetic material if it behaves like Earth's eukaryotic organisms?
options: Suspended freely in the cytoplasm only
Embedded within the lipid bilayer of the cell membrane
Stored securely inside the nucleus
Dissolved in the cell wall pores.

questions.question: A student is looking at a microscopic organism under a high-powered microscope. They note that the cell has a cell wall and cytoplasm, but lacks a nucleus. Where is its DNA located?
options: It does not have any DNA because it lacks a nucleus.
Its DNA is floating freely in the cytoplasm.
Its DNA is stored inside a chloroplast.
Its DNA is bound to the outer surface of the cell wall.

questions.question: How does the chemical structure of DNA function as an instructional manual for an organism's life processes?
options: The sequence of smaller molecules along the DNA chains forms a biological code used as instructions.
The physical weight of the DNA molecule determines which chemical reactions occur in the cytoplasm.
DNA acts as a filter that physically blocks harmful chemicals from entering the cell.
The temperature of the DNA molecule signals different proteins to break down.

questions.question: Why do biological siblings (not identical twins) usually look similar to each other and to their parents, but not exactly identical?
options: They inherit all of their genetic material from only one parent, which changes based on their diet.
They inherit different combinations of genetic material from both of their parents.
They only share environmental features and do not inherit any genetic material from parents.
Their genetic material is copied entirely from the mother, but modified by the father's environment.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about variation among offspring is correct?
options: Offspring from asexual reproduction are always genetically diverse, while sexual offspring are identical.
Identical twins are the only common exception to the rule that offspring vary and are not identical to their parents or siblings.
All offspring are exact copies of their fathers due to stronger genetic dominance.
Environmental factors completely prevent any genetic variation from appearing in offspring.

questions.question: A professional weightlifter develops extremely large muscles through intense training. If they have a child, why won't the child be born with exceptionally large muscles?
options: Muscular features are carried on non-coding DNA, which is never inherited.
Only features caused by instructions in the genetic material can be passed on to offspring.
The child will inherit the muscle size, but it only appears when they reach adulthood.
Muscle cells lack DNA entirely, so their features cannot be coded.

questions.question: Which of the following features is caused entirely by the environment and lifestyle, meaning it cannot be passed on to offspring?
options: A scar on a person's knee from falling off a bicycle.
The natural pigmentation and color of a person's eyes.
The shape of a person's earlobes.
The natural blood group of an individual.

questions.question: How did scientists eventually determine the three-dimensional double helix model of DNA in 1953?
options: A single scientist worked in complete isolation without looking at anyone else's data.
Scientists collected pieces of evidence, shared findings, and built upon each other's work.
They used a computer simulation that automatically generated the structure without physical data.
They copied the structure of a known protein and assumed DNA must be identical.

questions.question: What critical contribution did Rosalind Franklin's team make to the discovery of the structure of DNA in 1952?
options: They synthesized the first artificial DNA molecule in a test tube.
They used X-rays to produce a high-quality diffraction image of a DNA molecule.
They proved that bacteria do not contain any genetic material.
They discovered that DNA is located only in the cell membrane.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the fundamental chemical structure of a single DNA molecule?
options: It consists of two long chains of smaller chemical units joined together.
It is a single long protein chain folded into a complex three-dimensional shape.
It is composed of three interlocking carbohydrate rings linked by lipids.
It is a branched network of glucose molecules held together by weak hydrogen bonds.

questions.question: An organism's genome is best defined as which of the following?
options: Only the active genes that code for visible physical characteristics.
The complete set of all the DNA found within one of its cells.
The total mass of proteins produced by the organism throughout its life.
The genetic material inherited exclusively from the maternal parent.

questions.question: When visualizing the three-dimensional structure of a DNA molecule, how are the two chains arranged?
options: They run parallel to each other without any connections between them.
They are spiralled around one another in a double helix with cross-links.
They form a closed concentric circle with one chain completely inside the other.
They are folded into a series of flat, stacked sheets connected at the corners.

questions.question: Why is it that we can see DNA during a classroom extraction experiment, even though individual DNA molecules are invisible to the unaided eye?
options: The extraction process causes the DNA molecules to expand in size significantly.
The chemical reagents dye the individual DNA molecules to make them fluoresce.
Thousands of DNA molecules clump together during precipitation to form a visible mass.
The cell walls of the fruit merge with the DNA to form a thick, visible layer.

questions.question: How does the organization and storage of genetic material compare between a human cheek cell and a bacterium?
options: Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes in the nucleus, while bacteria have one chromosome in the cytoplasm.
Humans have 46 pairs of chromosomes in the cytoplasm, while bacteria have 23 single chromosomes in a nucleus.
Humans have a single circular chromosome in the nucleus, while bacteria have 23 pairs in the cytoplasm.
Both human cells and bacteria store 23 pairs of chromosomes inside a distinct nucleus.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the specific sections of DNA known as genes?
options: They form the physical outer membrane that protects the nucleus from damage.
They act as structural scaffolds that keep the chromosome tightly wound.
They store instructions for inherited features and essential life processes.
They serve as energy storage units that are broken down during respiration.

questions.question: If a section of DNA is identified as 'non-coding DNA', what role does it play in the cell?
options: It has no function at all and is eventually destroyed by cell enzymes.
It contains instructions that control when the information in genes is used.
It codes for the production of lipid molecules instead of proteins.
It is used to build the cell wall in both plant and animal cells.

questions.question: In which of the following groups of organisms is the genetic material stored inside a specialized, membrane-bound nucleus?
options: Plants, animals, and fungi
Bacteria, plants, and viruses
Animals, bacteria, and archaea
Fungi, bacteria, and protozoa without membranes

questions.question: A student looks at a bacterium under a microscope. Where is the bacterium's genetic material located, and why?
options: In the nucleus, because all living cells contain a nucleus to protect their DNA.
In the cytoplasm, because bacteria are microorganisms that lack a nucleus.
Inside the cell wall, because bacteria do not have cytoplasm.
Attached to the outer capsule, because bacteria lack internal genetic material.

questions.question: How does DNA act as an instruction manual for an organism's characteristics and functions?
options: By releasing electrical impulses directly to the cell membrane.
By acting as a chemical catalyst that speeds up physical movement.
By being built from molecules that form a code used to build features and control life processes.
By physically changing its shape to match the required structure of the cell.

questions.question: A pair of oak trees reproduce and produce acorns that grow into new oak trees. This species resemblance is a result of which biological concept?
options: Environmental adaptation during the offspring's early growth.
Organisms making offspring of the same kind when they reproduce.
Random changes in the soil nutrients where the seeds germinated.
The offspring copying the physical shape of nearby mature trees.

questions.question: Why do siblings in a family typically look similar to each other and their parents, but are not identical?
options: They inherit features from both parents, creating a unique combination of shared traits.
They share the exact same environment, which forces their physical features to align.
Children actively choose which physical characteristics to copy from their parents.
Only the father's genetic material is expressed in the offspring, limiting variation.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains how biological features are passed from parents to offspring during reproduction?
options: Offspring absorb nutrients containing physical traits from their parents' surroundings.
Genetic material containing instructions is transferred from parents to offspring.
Parents teach their offspring how to develop specific physical features.
The physical actions of the parents during their lifetime are copied by the offspring.

questions.question: A professional weightlifter develops large, strong muscles through years of intensive training. Why will their future children not be born with these enlarged muscles?
options: Muscle size is a trait that skips a generation in human inheritance.
Only features caused by instructions in the genetic material can be inherited.
Genetic material is only passed down from the mother, not the father.
The children's bodies will actively reject any traits related to physical strength.

questions.question: Why is a scar on a person's arm not passed on to their biological children?
options: Scars are caused by the environment and lifestyle, so they cannot be inherited.
The genetic material in the nucleus repairs itself before reproduction.
Scars are recessive genetic traits that require two copies to appear.
Environmental features are only inherited if they occur before adulthood.

questions.question: Which of the following timelines correctly describes the discovery of DNA and the determination of its structure?
options: DNA was discovered in 1953, and its structure was worked out the same year.
DNA was discovered in 1869, but scientists did not work out its structure until 1953.
DNA structure was modeled in 1869, but the substance itself was only found in 1953.
DNA was discovered by ancient philosophers, but named in 1952.

questions.question: How was the model of the double helix structure of DNA developed by scientists?
options: A single scientist worked in isolation to deduce the structure purely from theory.
Scientists collected evidence and shared their findings to collaboratively build the model.
It was discovered by accident when analyzing starch molecules under a light microscope.
It was proposed by a government committee without using experimental evidence.

questions.question: What crucial contribution did Rosalind Franklin’s team make to the discovery of DNA’s structure in 1952?
options: They built the first three-dimensional cardboard model of the double helix.
They used X-rays to produce an image of a DNA molecule.
They proved that DNA was not the genetic material of living organisms.
They extracted DNA from fruit cells for the very first time in history.

questions.question: How did James Watson from Cambridge obtain the key visual evidence needed to understand the shape of DNA?
options: He performed the X-ray crystallization experiments himself in his own laboratory.
He was shown the picture of DNA taken by Rosalind Franklin’s team by Maurice Wilkins.
He found the photograph published in a popular daily newspaper.
He drew a theoretical diagram that happened to match Franklin's image by chance.

questions.question: Who used the X-ray picture evidence to construct and complete the first accurate physical model of the DNA double helix?
options: Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins
James Watson and Francis Crick
Gregor Mendel and Charles Darwin
Louis Pasteur and Robert Hooke
